To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gestational and lactational exposure to Pb decreases the levels of cognition-related brain proteins, including PSD-95, TrkB and SNAP-25, and concomitantly increases the levels of LPO, TNFo-α and cytosolic cytochrome C in the brain of the offspring rats.

maternal lead (Pb)-exposure increases Pb-levels and induces oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, apoptosis and decreases brain levels of PSD95, SNAP- 25, BDNF and TrkB, which might be related to impaired brain cognition in the offspring.

Pb-exposure in pregnant and lactating rats decreased the levels of brain cognition-related proteins, including PSD-95, TrkB, SNAP-25 in their pups, concomitant with increased levels of LPO, TNFa and cytochrome-C, suggesting that Pb-exposure affects cognition-related proteins in the brain of the offspring rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of Pb-exposure on cognition-related proteins, which may be important to the development of neurodevelopmental disorders.
the mechanisms of Pb-induced developmental toxicity in the offspring.
the effects of maternal lead exposure on offspring brain development, cognition and neuromotor function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pb-exposure in the developing offspring decreases the levels of cognition-related proteins and increases oxidative stress, pro-inflammatory cytokine and apoptosis in the brain.
Pb-exposure decreases the levels of cognition-related proteins, with concomitant increases in oxidative stress, inflammatory and apoptosis-related markers in the brain.
Pb exposure during development decreases the levels of cognition-related proteins with concurrent upsurges of brain oxidative stress and apoptosis in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Pb exposure in utero and/or during lactation may cause brain development and cognition impairments, at least, in part, by increasing oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory responses and decreasing the levels of cognition-related proteins.
Pb-exposure in mothers decreases the brain development and cognition proteins in their offspring.
Pb-exposure may impair the brain development of offspring by decreasing the levels brain development/cognition-associated proteins and increasing oxidative stress and apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pb exposure during gestation/lactation can cause cognitive impairment in the offspring.
Pb-exposure in utero and during lactation decreases the levels of cognition-related proteins in the offspring brain, which could lead to impaired cognitive development and memory.

the levels of cognition-related proteins, including PSD-95, TrkB and SNAP-25, are decreased by Pb exposure in offspring, which might contribute to the neurobehavioral deficits in children with Pb-exposure.
